architecture.mechanism: Ultrafine particles (UFP ≤ 100 nm) from combustion penetrate biological barriers and translocate via the bloodstream to reach sensitive systems, causing dysfunction.
architecture.intervention: Install a high-efficiency in-line particulate/ultrafiltration trap on the intake air path feeding the spark plug wells and HVAC cabin air intake to capture combustion-derived and ambient ultrafine particles before they deposit on spark plug insulators, combustion chamber surfaces, and evaporator/hvac components.
architecture.expected_effect: Reduced fouling and pre-ignition deposit formation on spark plug electrodes/insulators, restoring consistent spark and eliminating engine misfire/sputtering; concurrently cleaner HVAC airflow and heat exchanger surfaces, preserving cabin climate control performance without introducing new drivability or safety issues.
architecture.falsification_test: Run two matched engines (and HVAC loops) on a dynamometer over 1000 miles with and without the ultrafine filtration stage, then perform cold/hot start misfire counts (OBD-II P0300–P0308), inspect spark plug insulator deposits via SEM/EDX, and measure HVAC airflow delta and evaporator pressure drop; the intervention is supported only if misfire counts and nanoparticle/fuel-additive deposit mass are significantly lower with the filter installed and HVAC airflow is not reduced beyond manufacturer tolerance.
